content:
Facts: The children of the deceased sued the sole heir of their late mother, alleging misappropriation of substantial sums during the deceased’s lifetime through withdrawals from personal and joint bank accounts and seeking restitution to the estate and an accounting; the defendant raised preliminary objections and filed counterclaims for reimbursement, insurance proceeds, and collation of alleged gifts.
Legal framework
Articles 533, 737, 1284, 177, 588, 733–734 of the Italian Civil Code on inheritance petition, collation, interest, community property, distinction between heir and legatee, and testamentary division; Articles 183, 96 CPC on preclusions and abusive litigation; principles on joint bank accounts, burden of proof, waiver of rights, and admissibility of claims.
Interpretative issue
Whether an heir who has expressly acknowledged receipt of her share and waived further claims retains standing to sue; whether alleged withdrawals from joint and personal accounts can be qualified as misappropriation or undue payments imputable to the estate; and whether late factual allegations and a belated action for reduction are admissible.
Principle applied
A beneficiary who has expressly acknowledged receipt of her inheritance share and broadly waived any further present or future claims lacks standing to bring subsequent restitution or accounting actions based on pre-existing facts. Claims for recovery of sums allegedly misappropriated during the deceased’s lifetime require strict proof that the assets belonged exclusively to the deceased at the opening of the succession; withdrawals from joint accounts are presumed to concern jointly owned funds unless the contrary is specifically alleged and proven. New factual allegations introduced after assertive preclusions under Article 183(6) CPC are inadmissible and cannot be remedied by documentary evidence. A late and generic action for reduction, previously waived and lacking precise indication of the estate, reserved shares, and prejudicial acts, is inadmissible. Collation obligations arise automatically upon succession and apply to proven lifetime gifts, with the burden on the donee-heir to specifically contest and prove impediments to collation. ID: ITI108; Instance_Type: First instance; Legal_Duration: P2Y3M; Law: IT – Civil Code – 588, 737, 1284(1); State: IT; Type: Succession; Costs: Heir 1, Heir 2 - 43643.65; Immovable_Assets: House; Movable_Assets: Bank transfers (177.250,00); Type_of_succession: Testamentary; Second part of full text: 
Indeed, the claim referred to in point (1) above is, according to some, a real action for inheritance (Article 533 of the Italian Civil Code), which '...is an action for conviction with a necessarily recuperative content, in that it is aimed at obtaining, subject to verification of the status of heir, the return of all or part of the inherited assets from anyone who possesses them without title or as an heir' (Court of Piacenza, 02/05/2018, (hearing 30/04/2018, filed 02/05/2018), no. 335; DeJure; a similar position also appears to have been expressed by the Court of Bergamo, Section I, 02/05/2022, DeJure2); recent case law has, however, expressed a contrary opinion, noting that '...the claim for restitution of the sums that the defendant allegedly withdrew from THE DECEASED's account, as joint account holder, ... does not fall within the scope of Article 22 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure as a 'petition'. With a petition, in fact, 'the heir can only claim the assets that he or she has inherited from the deceased, i.e. the assets that were included in the estate at the time of the opening of the succession; it follows that such an action cannot be brought to include in the succession sums of money that the deceased, prior to his death, remitted by means of bank cheques, without any apparent justification, to the future heir and which the latter has or had at his disposal by virtue of a pre-existing legal title independent of the death of the deceased" (Cass. No. 3181/2011). (Cass. Civ. Sez. 6 - 2, Order No. 11879 of 12/04/2022), taking into account the different configuration of the action as a claim for the repayment of an objective undue payment (see, Court of Taranto, 09/02/2022, No. 328; DeJure), for payments without justification (see Cass. Civ. Sez. 2 - , Judgment no. 30713 of 27/11/2018). In the opinion of the plaintiffs, on 12/10/2012, Ms SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED appropriated the sum of €1 million by means of a transfer from Banca Mediolanum (see writ of summons, doc. 12, plaintiff's file); as a claim for the recovery of an undue payment, from an evidentiary point of view, 'the claimant creditor has the burden of proving the facts constituting its claim: both the payment made and the lack of a cause justifying it. This general principle also applies in cases where recovery is sought only for part of the
payment made" (Court of Velletri, Section II, 29/04/2022, No. 882, DeJure); moreover, if qualified as an inheritance petition, on an objective level, "...the burden of proof, within the limits relating to the defence of the counterparty, of the belonging of the asset to the estate at the time of the opening of the succession" remains unchanged (Court of Bergamo, Section I, 02/05/2022, No. 679, DeJure). On this point, the defendant objects that the sums in the current accounts held in the name of or jointly held by THE DECEASED belonged to THE DECEASED and SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED, as they were married under the community property regime, so the plaintiffs would be required to prove that any transactions carried out by Ms SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED involved more than half of the joint assets. On this point, pursuant to Article 177(1) of the Italian Civil Code, 'The profits from the personal activity of both spouses fall into the joint estate, unless the activity is carried out before or after the cohabitation or in the absence of it. The fruits of the property of each spouse, the revenues, whether due as pension or income, from both personal and joint property, and the profits from joint property companies fall into the joint estate. The defendant points out that the money deposited in the accounts comes from the salaries paid to both spouses by Cassa Rurale di Civitella, and therefore, as profits from personal activity, was jointly owned by the spouses; there is documentary evidence on this point (see docs. 7 to 10 of the defendant's file), demonstrating payments by the bank to THE DECEASED and SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED for work performed in joint ownership. Moreover, in relation to the bank accounts indicated by the plaintiff as sources of the sum of €1 million, which in the opinion of the defendant would not have belonged to THE DECEASED, it should be noted that: (1) for account no. 549991, held solely in the name of THE DECEASED, it is proven that on 12 October 2012 the account was financed through transfers from the joint account no. 1091672 (doc. 15, defendant's file); (2) for account no. 1091672, held jointly by THE DECEASED and SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED, it is proven by the documents produced by the defendant that the bank account was financed over the years by both spouses, with salary deposits and transfers between accounts (docs. 11 to 14, defendant's file). Therefore, for the operation carried out on 12 October 2012, no violation of Article 184 of the Italian Civil Code can be detected – in relation to the transfer to account no. 549991 from the joint account no. 1091672 – given that the transfer was carried out on a fully financed account; in fact, contrary to the plaintiff's assertions, from the documents produced it is not proven that the transaction on 12 October 2012 concerned only money directly deposited by THE DECEASED in the account. Furthermore, for the first instalment of €1 million, subject of the transfer on 12 October 2012 from account no. 549991, subscribed to the TM 1747485 fund, it is proven by the documents produced by the defendant (see doc. 23 to 28, 37, 38 of the defendant's file) that subsequent
divestments were aimed at making other investments, again in favour of THE DECEASED and his wife, so that the plaintiff's claims regarding the disappearance of the sum are not proven. It should also be noted that the power of attorney (doc. 14 plaintiff's file) produced by the plaintiff only proves the power of attorney given by THE DECEASED to SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED to act for and on his behalf in carrying out bank transactions, subject to the duty to account; however, it does not prove that the conduct was actually carried out in violation of said duty to account, which is contested by the defendant, who, in the alternative, to justify and prove the legitimacy of the conduct, also produced, at the first hearing, documents 6 to 13, which – as the defendant points out – prove the existence of joint ownership of the money in the accounts in question, originating from joint payments made by THE DECEASED and SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED. However, as a result of the production, the plaintiffs did not object or modify their initial thesis, proceeding only to a contestation pursuant to Article 214 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure, which was deemed unfounded by the GI, again in the order of 5 August 2021. It should also be noted that the plaintiffs failed to contest in a timely manner the conduct set out in the narrative and, in particular, failed to specify for each and every conduct alleged and relating to the second chapter, that is, payments to third parties, in favour of which subject and on what basis the conduct was alleged to be illegitimate, an allegation that instead appears to be produced, belatedly, and partially, in the second brief pursuant to Article 183(6) of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure (see specifically point 2 on page 3). Moreover, in the above-mentioned brief, the plaintiffs do not contest the objection formulated by the defendant regarding the nature of the joint assets and the burden of proof, merely observing that (1) as they are the party requesting payment, they have satisfied the burden of proof, by means of the introduction of document no. 2, which documents a request for statements of account, and document no. 3, which documents the declaration of succession; (2) they furthermore produced an additional witness list for questioning on the defendant's circumstances and objects, in relation to the existence of joint ownership of the funds in the accounts indicated in the aforementioned documents produced at the first hearing, as well as a list of witnesses to be heard to refute the alleged joint ownership. However, the plaintiffs do not dispute the issue of ownership by producing specific documents, nor do they reformulate their own request for the production of documents, by way of derogation from Article 210 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure, to a specific bank or credit institution. Therefore, the plaintiffs have not succeeded in proving, with regard to the accounts indicated above as the source of the sum that was the subject of the transfer on 12 October 2012 in favour of the TM 1747485 fund, that the amounts came from THE DECEASED and therefore belonged to him alone, or that more than half came from THE DECEASED, therefore falling outside the joint ownership of SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED; the plaintiffs have also not proven, beyond a reasonable doubt, the alleged unlawful appropriation of said sum by SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED, which, as already mentioned, was also subsequently invested in favour of
THE DECEASED and his wife. In light of the above observations, it must be considered that the plaintiffs have not succeeded in proving the grounds for their claim in relation to the aforementioned sum of €1 million. As for the second instalment of €250,000.00, which was allegedly the subject of unlawful appropriation, the defendant points out that there was no unlawful appropriation as it consisted of a cheque drawn on a joint account and credited to another joint account, which, as already observed, contained assets belonging to both THE DECEASED and SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED. On this point, the plaintiffs object that, in any case, on 1 December 2016, SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED subscribed, solely on her behalf, to the TM 1986278 fund for the sum of €250,000.00, thus preventing THE DECEASED from accessing this sum, even indirectly. However, in the opinion of the Court, THE DECEASED, who died on ..., the day before the above-mentioned subscription on 1 December 2016 (see doc. 3, plaintiff's file), could never have accessed the sum following the subscription, as he had already passed away; it is also not proven that THE DECEASED, at the time of his death, had expressed any intention to access the sum, which remained, as jointly owned, and as such reported in the declaration of succession, which is due to SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED and the heirs. The plaintiffs, as already mentioned, also claim that SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED carried out a series of operations on the accounts for her own benefit, in order to deviate THE DECEASED's assets. On this point, the defendant asserts that the parties acted by mutual agreement, as evidenced by the reciprocal payments and transfers between them over time, which clearly show a regular and constant administration of the accounts by both spouses without objection from either of them, as documented by the defendant with documents 6 to 13. The plaintiffs object that THE DECEASED was not in a position to understand the economic and financial acts in question, given his cognitive conditions starting from 2009, as alleged in point 12) of the request for oral evidence filed in relation to the second brief pursuant to Article 183(6) of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure, a chapter that was, however, excluded by the GI, having been considered to be lacking in specificity regarding the circumstances to be proven and belatedly introduced. Moreover, the objection is refuted by the documentary evidence (see docs. 1, 4, 14 plaintiff's file) which, in the opinion of the defendant (see point 4, page 2 of the first brief pursuant to Article 183(6) of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure, defendant) demonstrates that THE DECEASED, until two months before his death, was lucid and aware of his actions, and the plaintiffs have not proven the contrary. It should also be noted that the plaintiffs, in relation to this chapter relating to the deviations carried out to the detriment of THE DECEASED, have not proven which and how many of these deviations concerned solely the assets of THE DECEASED, nor, conversely, that all the deviations cannot be justified as concerned jointly owned assets, nor that they were carried out against the will of THE DECEASED; in fact, the plaintiffs only allege that, in principle and abstractly, SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED, in her capacity as attorney, could not dispose of THE DECEASED's assets as if they were her own and in favour of third parties. The plaintiffs' objection also does not appear to be supported by the request for production of documents and for admitting the list of witnesses contained in the second brief pursuant to Article 183(6) of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure, which was rejected by the GI, as it was deemed to be lacking in specificity in the case of the list of witnesses and, in the case of the request for production of documents, because it was generic and did not identify specific debtors (so-called 'fishing expedition'), in relation to the charges indicated by the plaintiffs in documents 6, 7, 9, relating to the alleged beneficiaries THIRD PARTY 9, THIRD PARTY 10, THIRD PARTY 1 sas, THIRD PARTY 11 (see docs. 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 42); however, on reading these documents, there is no evidence that the charges carried by these cheques can be attributed to the above-mentioned non-joint current account. Finally, the cheque in doc. 42 is made out to a bank other than Mediolanum.
Therefore, the grounds for the recovery and accounting action brought by the plaintiffs have not been proven, and the claims must be dismissed.
The counterclaims brought by the defendant remain to be analysed.
The first counterclaim seeks reimbursement by the plaintiff HEIR 1 of the amount of €150,000.00, equal to his share of the sum of €300,000.00, allegedly advanced by the defendant for the settlement of HEIR 4's share. In the plaintiff's opinion, the payment was made with money from the estate. The claim is well-founded, given that an examination of document 2 produced by the defendant shows that the debit was made from Banca Mediolanum current account no. -4704, held solely in the name of SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED and not indicated in the declaration of succession (plaintiff's document 3).
The defendant's second counterclaim concerns the sum of €207,000.00 collected by the plaintiff under a Generali Ass.ni policy taken out by THE DECEASED and naming Ms SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED and Mr HEIR 1 as beneficiaries, but collected only by the latter. In the plaintiff's opinion, the share was attributed to the plaintiff by Ms SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED as a gift. The exception does not appear to be proven, especially since any donation, even if it had been made, would be null and void due to a defect in form. The counterclaim is therefore well founded.
The third counterclaim concerns the portion of the 2015 income tax that was allegedly collected in full by the plaintiff HEIR 1 and never credited back. The claim is contested and based on documentation (doc. 10, doc. 30 defendant's file) which, however, does not prove that the plaintiff actually collected the refund. The claim is therefore unfounded and must be rejected.
The fourth counterclaim concerns the plaintiff's request for the restoration of the estate through collation of gifts allegedly received for approximately £240,000.00. In the defendant's opinion, the plaintiff received bank transfers and cheques constituting gifts, which are subject to collation. In this regard, it should be noted that case law has highlighted that 'The prerequisite for the obligation of collation, pursuant to Article 737 of the Italian Civil Code, is that the person subject to it has received assets or rights as gifts from the deceased, either directly or indirectly through payments made by the latter' (Civil Cassation, Section 6 - 2, Order No. 1506 of 22/01/2018). In particular, 'In the case of gifts made during the lifetime of the deceased, the collation of the estate - in both forms provided for by law, by transfer of the asset in kind or by imputation - is a legal instrument aimed at forming the estate to be divided in order to ensure balance and equal treatment among the various co-heirs, so as not to alter the value ratio between the various shares, to be determined in relation to the extent of each co-heir's right, on the basis of the sum of the 'relictum' and the 'donatum' at the time of the opening of the succession, and thus guaranteeing each of the heirs the possibility of obtaining a quantity of assets proportionate to their share. It follows that the obligation of collation arises automatically following the opening of the succession' (Civil Cassation, Section 2, Judgment No. 15131 of 18/07/2005 (Rv. 582041 - 01); the persons required to make the collation are the children and their descendants and the spouse who are entitled to the succession (Article 737 of the Italian Civil Code). This circumstance is contested by the opposing party in the minutes of the hearing of 14 July 2021. The following are documented in the records:
doc. 18) cheque for the amount of €30,000.00 drawn on Banca di Forlì credito cooperativo: the copy produced in the proceedings is illegible as regards the payee and the signature, so that the relevant amount cannot be counted;
doc. 19) transfer order dated 19 July 2011 by THE DECEASED and SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED, for a total of €10,000.00 in favour of the plaintiff, reason for payment 'ordinary expenses'; as the order comes from a joint account, the sum of €5,000.00 may be assessed as a gift subject to collation, in relation to which, however, the plaintiff's objection appears to be completely unfounded and generic, in contrast to the burden of the person called upon to collate to object precisely and provide evidence of the fact preventing collation (see Civil Cassation Section II, 01/02/1995, no. 1159): the plaintiff is therefore required to collate the amount of €5,000.00;
doc. 20) transfer order dated 27 December 2011 by THE DECEASED and SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED, for a total of €3,000.00 in favour of the plaintiff, reason for payment 'deposit'; as the order comes from a joint account, the sum of €1,500.00 may be considered as a gift subject to collation, in relation to which, however, the plaintiff's objection appears to be completely unfounded and generic, in contrast to the burden of the person called upon to collate to object precisely and provide evidence of the fact preventing collation (see Civil Cassation Section II, 01/02/1995, no. 1159): the plaintiff is therefore required to collate the amount of €1,500.00;
doc. 21) transfer order dated 12 October 2012 by THE DECEASED and SPOUSE OF THE DECEASED, for a total of €1,500.00 in favour of the plaintiff, reason for payment 'transfer'; as the order comes from a joint account, the sum of €750.00 may be considered as a gift subject to collation, in relation to which, however, the plaintiff's objection appears to be completely unfounded and generic, in contrast to the burden of the person called upon to collate to object precisely and provide evidence of the impediment to collation (see Civil Cassation Section II, 01/02/1995, no. 1159): the plaintiff is therefore required to collate the amount of €750.00;
doc. 22) transfer order from THE DECEASED to HEIR 1, for the amount of €50,000.00, reason 'as agreed', dated 31/03/2009: also for this order, the plaintiff's objection appears to be completely unfounded and generic, in contrast with the burden of the person called upon to pay to object precisely and provide evidence of the fact preventing payment (see Civil Cassation Section II, 01/02/1995, no. 1159): the plaintiff is therefore required to collate the amount of €50,000.00;
doc. 23) transfer order from THE DECEASED to HEIR 1, for the amount of €50,000.00, reason 'as agreed', dated 29 December 2008: also for this order, the plaintiff's objection appears to be completely unfounded and generic, in contrast with the burden of the person called upon to make the collation to object precisely and provide evidence of the fact preventing the collation (see Civil Cassation Section II, 01/02/1995, no. 1159); the plaintiff is therefore required to collate the amount of €50,000.00;
doc. 24) transfer in favour of HEIR 1 from an account in the name of THE DECEASED for the amount of €30,000.00 on 29/02/2012: also for this provision, the plaintiff's objection appears to be completely unfounded and generic, in contrast with the burden of the person called upon to make the collation to object precisely and provide evidence of the fact preventing the collation (see Civil Cassation Section II, 01/02/1995, no. 1159); the plaintiff is therefore required to collate the amount of €30,000.00;
doc. 25) transfer by THE DECEASED to HEIR 1 from an account held in the name of THE DECEASED for the sum of €20,000.00 on 14 February 2013: also for this provision, the plaintiff's objection appears to be completely unfounded and generic, in contrast with the burden of the person called upon to collate to object precisely and provide evidence of the fact preventing collation (see Civil Cassation Section II, 01/02/1995, no. 1159); the plaintiff is therefore required to collate the amount of €20,000.00;
doc. 26) transfer by THE DECEASED to HEIR 1 from an account in the name of THE DECEASED for the sum of €20,000.00 on 3 September 2013: also for this provision, the plaintiff's objection appears to be completely unfounded and generic, in contrast with the burden of the person called upon to make the collation to object precisely and provide evidence of the fact preventing the collation (see Civil Cassation Section II, 01/02/1995, no. 1159); the plaintiff is therefore required to collate the amount of €20,000.00;
doc. 27) transfer order dated 10 October 2016: not subject to collation as it is subsequent to the death;
total €177,250.00 total to be paid to the defendant (50%): €88,625.00.
The counterclaim for collation is therefore upheld, limited to the above amount.
With regard to interest and revaluation, interest is due on the above amounts pursuant to Article 1284(1) of the Italian Civil Code (as this is a non-contractual matter) from the date of the legal claim to the date of settlement. No revaluation is due, as the reimbursements and contributions requested follow the nominalistic principle, with the consequent exclusion of revaluation (see Civil Court, Section 2, Judgment No. 26486 of 17 October 2019).
The costs of the present proceedings shall be borne by the unsuccessful party and shall be settled in accordance with the provisions of Ministerial Decree 55 of 2014, average parameters for the bracket corresponding to the value of the case, excluding the mediation phase, as this does not appear to be effectively independent of the strict instrumentality of the merits phase.
The conditions for the sentence pursuant to Article 96 of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure requested by the defendant do not exist.
P.Q.M.
The Judge of the Court of Forlì, sitting in panel, definitively ruling on case no. 3764 of 2020 RG, rejecting all other and contrary motions, claims and objections, hereby orders as follows:
Rejects the objection of nullity of the writ of summons;
Ascertains and declares the lack of standing to sue on the part of HEIR 2, for the reasons detailed in the grounds;
Declares the plaintiffs' request for reduction inadmissible;
Rejects all further claims made by the plaintiffs;
Partially upholds the counterclaims brought by HEIR 3 and therefore orders HEIR 1 to pay HEIR 3, on this basis and for the reasons set out in the introduction, the total sum of €445,625.00 plus interest pursuant to Article 1284(1) of the Italian Civil Code from the date of the legal claim to the date of settlement;
Orders HEIR 1 and HEIR 2, jointly and severally, to reimburse HEIR 3 in full for the costs of the present proceedings, which it sets at a total of €37,951.00 for fees, plus 15% for general expenses, postage and VAT as required by law.
Forlì, 20 March 2023
The President The Judge
